channel.description: Latest articles from The Local France (thelocal.fr)

item.title: ANALYSIS: Who's who in France's 2027 presidential election race
item.description: With local elections out of the way, attention is turning to next year's presidential race - in April and May 2027, French people will go to the polls and pick their next president. Here's how the race is shaping up so far.

item.title: What steps is France taking to mitigate fuel price rises?
item.description: France's government announced some indirect measures Monday to alleviate fuel price rises resulting from the Middle East war, while asking refiners if they were able to boost their output.

item.title: French Expression of the Day: Tomber à pic
item.description: This French expression has its roots in the origins of tennis...

item.title: OPINION: Local elections show French far right is beatable - but not by this squabbling opposition
item.description: This was a Mr Potato Head election - writes John Lichfield - pick different features of the municipal results on Sunday and you can give France the face of your choosing.

item.title: Explained: When the French use 'allô' versus 'bonjour'
item.description: Have you ever wondered why French people say 'allô' on the phone? It sounds like 'hello' but is spelt differently... so where does it come from? Find out how it's used by native speakers in everyday conversations.

item.title: French judge investigates ex-EU border chief for complicity in crimes
item.description: A French judge will investigate claims brought by an NGO that the former head of the European Union border agency, Frontex, was complicit in crimes against humanity, a judicial source told AFP on Tuesday.

item.title: French teachers call nationwide strike over budget cuts
item.description: Five of France's largest teaching unions have called a nationwide strike in protest at what they describe as 'austerity' budget plans for education.

item.title: Which countries in Europe have the biggest share of foreign residents?
item.description: In 2025, people born outside the European Union made up about 10 percent of the EU’s 450 million population. But which countries have the largest share of foreign-born residents?

item.title: 'It seems very unfair': Key questions answered on French citizenship changes
item.description: France's rules on citizenship have undergone several big changes in the last year - so we held a live Q&A to answer the key questions from members of The Local. Here's a roundup of the main topics.

item.title: French government expands obligatory wildfire prevention work for homeowners
item.description: Laws require many homeowners in the south of France to do compulsory works each year to help prevent the spread of wildfires - but as fires become more common, the laws have been expanded to cover properties in northern France, including Brittany.

item.title: New Nice mayor poses a 'real problem' for 2030 Winter Olympics
item.description: The 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps, already bedevilled by several senior executives quitting, faces another potential headache with the election of far-right politician Eric Ciotti as mayor of Nice.

item.title: 600-year-old pinot noir grape found in medieval French toilet
item.description: A 600-year-old grape seed discovered in the toilets of a medieval French hospital is genetically identical to the grapes still being used to make pinot noir wine, scientists said on Tuesday.
